title: TV debates in EP election campaigns – the influence of the 2019 Eurovision debate on voting behaviour

link_reviews.note: The findings provide examples of media, information, and campaign-contact exposure linked to debate viewing or electoral turnout. These are sufficiently coherent as information/communication exposure; the narrower settings and forms of exposure do not require splitting the group.
Five independent undeniable papers reached the stop rule.
All pinned findings on this link were reviewed.
The confounder's other link (category-tech-usage->political-debate-exposure) has no retained finding, so there is no confounding path and this link needed no further review.

The finding directly links individual exposure to the 2019 Eurovision debate with individual turnout in the 2019 European Parliament election, matching the focal exposure, outcome, and target population.

confounders.reason: The focal Model 5 includes c9, general media exposure, as a pre-treatment proxy for the broad information and media exposure confounder. It is a reasonable proxy for respondents’ overall access to and exposure to political information, but may not capture specific campaign messages or particular content they encountered. The separate post-debate media-coverage measure, c15, is an intervening variable and does not count as confounder control.

No supported confounding path: every finding on this confounder's link to the exposure was excluded, so it cannot confound the focal relationship. This status was set from the findings alone; the paper's specification was not reviewed for it.

The snapshot's turnout group captures electoral participation generally; it is not restricted to the particular 2019 European Parliament election, countries, or self-report measure.
